title: Insecure Password Storage
description: Passwords are stored using weak or reversible mechanisms, such as plaintext, unsalted hashes, fast general-purpose hashes (MD5, SHA-1), or reversible encryption. If the data store is exposed, these credentials can be recovered quickly through offline cracking, undermining the protection passwords are meant to provide.
businessImpact: High --- exposure of the credential store can lead to mass account compromise, and reused passwords extend the impact to other systems and services.
remediation:
- Hash passwords with a modern, slow, salted algorithm such as Argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt.
- Never store passwords in plaintext or with reversible encryption.
- Apply a unique random salt per password and consider a secret pepper.
- Rehash and migrate existing weakly-stored credentials on next login.
